source.title: A Fine-Grained Spectral Perspective on Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no obvious truncation or garbling that prevents reading.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains MLPs under controlled depth, layer-training, activation, and input-distribution conditions, and reports effects on training loss or test error. These results bear conceptually on depth and training outcomes, though the experiments are largely regression and generalization studies rather than the classification-error claim as stated.
record.gate_note: The study reports training procedures and outcomes that bear on V3's depth and shortcut-related setting and V5's learning-rate behavior, but it does not test identity shortcuts, above-stability recovery, or training classification error. Rows below capture separately reported best test errors by dataset and training mode. Figure 5 learning-rate comparisons are not rows because they report maximal nondiverging learning rates, not training loss/error outcomes named by a claim version.
record.test_reason: The study reports generalization and maximum nondiverging learning rates, but does not measure the training effects specified by any version. Figure 7 measures best test error, not V3's training-error degradation. Figure 5 shows finite networks tolerating rates above an infinite-width prediction, but does not establish V5's loss-rise, curvature-drop and low-loss recovery sequence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that neural-kernel spectra provide insights into initialization and generalization; fractional variance is a rough predictor of test loss, and spectral theory also helps predict maximum nondiverging learning rates. Their experiments demonstrate task-dependent optimal depth.
record.recipe_differences: Controlled MLP experiments using CK/NTK and square-loss regression or dataset label regression; no direct reproduction of the classification-error or residual-shortcut recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, training only the last layer versus all layers, activation, and dataset affect reported performance trends.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 reports optimal depths for best test error on MNIST and CIFAR-10: depth 1 when training only the last layer and approximately 5 when training all layers, across 10 seeds. These are generalization outcomes and cannot establish V3's training-error degradation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested ReLU MLP recipes, best test error worsens as depth moves away from an intermediate optimum.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 5 and 9 compare predicted and empirical maximum nondiverging learning rates. All-layer training often tolerates rates above the infinite-width NTK prediction, especially at greater depth. Appendix E.2 determines nondivergence over 1,000 iterations; it does not establish low-loss recovery or its curvature mechanism.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite-width MLPs can tolerate learning rates above an infinite-width kernel stability prediction, with prediction accuracy depending on training mode and preprocessing.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 3, 6 and 8 measure best validation loss for polynomial targets, showing dependence on target degree, depth and which layers are trained. They do not measure the training outcomes named by the versions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Target complexity affects optimal depth and the generalization advantage of training all layers rather than only the last layer.

record.problems: The depth-sweep outcomes relevant to V3 are presented in Figure 7 without numeric values in the supplied text; the reported outcome is best test error rather than training classification error. Most synthetic training experiments use one or ten seeds depending on figure.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7 reports depth-specific best test errors for MNIST and CIFAR10, but the supplied text gives only qualitative descriptions and figure-only plotted values; no rows were created because the values cannot be transcribed as stated numbers. Figure 5 reports maximum learning rates, which do not directly measure a version's named training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including corrupted or random labels and the specified failure conditions.
Spurious-local-minimum frequencies and their reduction through extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth through preserved signals and gradients, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
Above-threshold loss-rise and recovery with falling curvature; low final training loss; full-batch edge-of-stability trajectories; and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization comparisons measuring training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's designation of V3 as tested_not_extracted to not tested. No rows were supplied, so no row corrections are needed. The lack of numerical Figure 7 values does not create a missing result for V3 because its reported measure is test error.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR classification training error, random or corrupted labels, width, SGD/Adam classification outcomes, and small-model or early-stopping failures are not tested.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization or spurious-local-minimum rates are tested.

The paper tests depth effects on MNIST and CIFAR10 best test error for plain MLPs, but does not report training classification error or compare plain networks with identity shortcuts. The depth-sweep outcomes are shown only in Figure 7, without numeric values in the supplied text.
No activation-matched initialization or trainable-depth comparison is tested.
The paper predicts and measures maximum nondiverging learning rates, but does not test the described above-stability loss-rise and recovery or edge-of-stability behavior.
No batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparison is tested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
